findings.criterion: AC4 [non-codebase] — Reproduce the collision (dispatch near a schedule boundary) and demonstrate both runs surviving, or the dispatch being refused with a clear reason. A fix not exercised against the real collision has not been shown to work.
findings.detail: AC4 is tagged [non-codebase] and requires a concrete attestation demonstrating the collision was reproduced and both runs survived (or the dispatch was refused with a clear reason). The ticket's last comment names Gerrit 2950 (Verified+1, merged) and CI run_id 34437468052 (status: passed), but these describe the CI run for the fix itself — not a live reproduction of the collision scenario (a dispatch near a 6-hour schedule boundary with both runs surviving). The ticket's own completion evidence section explicitly acknowledges this gap: 'forcing GitHub cron jitter near a six-hour schedule boundary is not a deterministic local code exercise.' No attestation in the ticket snapshot describes the specific scenario of dispatching near a schedule boundary and observing both runs survive. The specifics present (Gerrit 2950, run 34437468052) substantiate that the fix was merged and CI passed, but do not substantiate the collision-reproduction requirement the criterion states.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment naming: (1) a specific GitHub Actions run URL or run ID for a `workflow_dispatch` on `main` that was dispatched near a 6-hour schedule boundary, (2) the concurrent scheduled run URL/ID, (3) the observed outcome showing both runs completed (or the dispatch was refused with a clear reason), and (4) the timestamp of the observation. This would satisfy the 'reproduce the collision' requirement with verifiable specifics.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
